overall_summary: Analysis across 47 deduplicated Shorts shows clear divergence: first-person immersive 'What If You Fell Into [Extreme Phenomenon]?' and extreme exoplanet survival concepts consistently dominate the channel's top tier (800–1,050+ views, 20–38 likes). Conversely, repeated identical uploads ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', 'Why Space Is Completely Silent') and standard trivia without narrative stakes (psychology tips, repeating octopus/shark trivia) stall below 100 views.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,028 views, 38 likes), 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (823 views, 15 likes), and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) yield the channel's highest retention and like-to-view ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Anchor hooks around sensory, high-stakes bodily peril or surreal what-if scenarios, retaining the 19–21s sweet spot with progressive reveals.

winning_patterns.evidence: Recent release 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' drove 980 views and 21 likes, while 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' earned 1,027 views and 36 likes.
winning_patterns.action: Frame cosmic facts as paradoxes or impossible realities that force the viewer to question basic physical laws.

weak_patterns.pattern: Repeated Re-uploads and Static Trivia Hooks
weak_patterns.evidence: Duplicate uploads of 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' dropped from 220 to 34 views; 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' flatlined at 5–10 views across multiple uploads.
weak_patterns.action: Eliminate direct re-uploads; retire low-arousal psychology trivia unless framed through an urgent micro-story or high-stakes scenario.

weak_patterns.pattern: Textbook Biological Facts Without High-Stakes Storytelling
weak_patterns.evidence: 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' averaged ~100–360 views with near-zero initial engagement despite three separate postings.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot biological subjects into 'cinematic animal survival' micro-stories rather than passive anatomy trivia.
